name: AW Proxy
description: Browser cookie proxy: an HTTP CONNECT proxy the AW Browser tunnels through, plus the cookie-sync API (/sync-cookies, /clear-cookies) that the aw-sync browser extensions (Chrome + iOS/Safari) push the user's real-browser cookies through, and encrypted persistence of chosen cookies in Postgres so they survive a proxy restart. aw-app-browser depends on this app for authentication.

proxy_port.description: TCP port the CONNECT-tunnel / cookie-sync HTTP server listens on. The aw-app-browser container's Chrome must be configured to tunnel through host:this-port.

browser_cdp_list_url.description: CDP /json/list endpoint of the browser this proxy injects/clears cookies into via WebSocket CDP commands. INTEGRATION TBD: this default mirrors the old hard-coded tools/browser/ container-Chrome port; it has not yet been reconciled with aw-app-browser's new Tier-2 (podman container, CDP behind the /api/apps/browser/* reverse proxy) — see this app's README.

allowed_networks.description: CIDR ranges allowed to use the CONNECT tunnel (the AW Browser container's source IP must be inside one of these).

dependencies.note: Declared here for documentation — the runtime does not yet resolve/enforce app dependencies (no such mechanism exists in src/apps/ as of 2026-07-28). aw-app-browser declares the reverse edge in its own aw-app.json.dependencies.apps.
